question: What is original sin, according to Catholic teaching?

choices.A: The sin committed by Adam, contracted (not imitated) by all his descendants, resulting in loss of sanctifying grace and a disordered human nature
choices.B: A personal sin each person commits at the first moment of moral awareness
choices.C: An evil force that inhabits the body but not the soul
choices.D: A symbolic story with no literal theological content

teaching.title: Original Sin
teaching.body: Original sin is not a sin each individual commits but a condition inherited from Adam. The Council of Trent (1546) defined that through Adam's sin: (1) death and suffering entered the world; (2) the whole person is wounded — intellect darkened, will weakened, passions disordered (concupiscence); (3) sanctifying grace is lost. This is 'contracted not committed.' Baptism removes original sin's guilt and restores grace, though concupiscence (the inclination to sin) remains. Paul's argument in Romans 5:12-21 is the primary scriptural basis.
